column1: # THE PARITY LEDGER -- known TypeScript/Go divergences. THIS FILE SHOULD
# NORMALLY BE EMPTY OF ROWS.
# test/spec/*.tsv is the contract: a row lives there only once BOTH
# implementations satisfy it. This file is the debt register for the
# opposite case -- a behaviour where the two ports are known to DISAGREE,
# recorded so the disagreement is visible and tracked instead of being
# rediscovered, and so nobody baselines one engine's output as the shared
# contract by accident.
# It is deliberately a .tsv living beside the suite, so it is read
# whenever the spec is read. Both runners (ts/test/spec.test.ts and
# go/spec_test.go) glob test/spec/*.tsv and skip comment and blank lines,
# so a file of comments contributes zero rows and asserts nothing.
# HOW TO USE IT
# A divergence is a BUG, not a feature. The default response is to fix
# the engine, not to write here. Add an entry ONLY when the divergence
# cannot be fixed from this repository right now -- e.g. it originates in
# a pinned @tabnas dependency, or the correct behaviour is an open
# language-design question.
# An entry MUST carry:
#   1. an issue reference (the tracking issue for the fix), and
#   2. a reason it is not simply fixed, and
#   3. the exact divergent inputs and BOTH engines' outputs.
# An entry is removed -- not amended -- when the divergence is fixed, and
# the behaviour then earns real rows in the appropriate spec file.
# Entries carry NO data rows: a row here would be executed by both
# runners and, by definition, could not pass in both. Everything below is
# commentary.
# 1. INTEGER-KIND VALUES ABOVE 2^53 THAT NEED MORE THAN 17 SIGNIFICANT
#    DIGITS TO WRITE EXACTLY
#    issue: #21
#    reason: this is the storage difference between the two ports, not a
#      local formatting slip. TS holds an integer-kind peg as a JS
#      number (a float64) and renders it with Number.toString, which
#      emits the SHORTEST decimal that round-trips (at most 17
#      significant digits). Go holds it as an int64 and renders the
#      exact value with strconv.FormatInt. Both denote the same float64,
#      but the text differs.
#    detail: only integer KIND is affected. A number-kind value goes
#      through the shared JS-Number.toString formatter in both ports
#      (go/scalar.go formatNumber), so the extreme-magnitude rows in
#      scalar.tsv and number-model.tsv are unaffected -- 2^63 written
#      0x8000000000000000, for one, which R1 makes number kind because
#      it is one past int64's maximum. (This clause used to cite
#      0x7fffffffffffffff instead. That literal is no longer a value in
#      either port: it is 2^63-1, it rounds UP to 2^63, and Phase 6
#      refuses it -- see number-model.tsv:hex-max-int64-lossy-err.)
#      Values whose exact digits fit in 17 significant digits agree:
#      Values needing more do not:
#      (Same divergence in gen and in canon.)
#    CORRECTION -- the resolution this entry used to record is WRONG,
#      and its own examples disprove it. It said that the number
#      tower's Phase 6 (a lossy integer literal becomes a located
#      error) "removes the divergence by refusing the input in both
#      ports", because "every input in this window is exactly such a
#      literal". It is not. Phase 6 refuses a literal that is not
#      EXACTLY REPRESENTABLE in binary64; it does not refuse one that
#      is merely large -- the rule is exactness, not magnitude, which is
#      the same correction the Phase 6 spec rows record for the hex
#      literals. Both values listed above are exact (2^60, and 2^63-1024
#      where the binary64 spacing is 1024), both still parse in both
#      ports with Phase 6 landed, and both still render differently.
#      Re-probed against both engines after Phase 4 and Phase 6 landed.
#      D6's exact integer sums open a SECOND route into the same window,
#      from operands Phase 6 accepts -- both of these are sums of powers
#      of two, so every literal involved is exact:
#      The second lands exactly ON int64's minimum, so it satisfies the
#      integer storage contract and is stored rather than refused. That
#      is why number-tower.tsv pins the POSITIVE int64-overflow sum
#      (2^62+2^62, which both ports refuse) and leaves this negative
#      mirror unpinned: no spec row may be written in this window.
#    what is true now: after Phase 6, every case that still diverges is
#      one where both ports hold EXACTLY the value the source asked for.
#      The old objection -- "making the two agree on text would only
#      agree on a wrong number" -- therefore no longer applies, and
#      neither does the instruction not to close this by choosing a
#      renderer: there is now a right answer, and Go already prints it.
#      Closing this entry means rendering an integer-kind peg by its
#      exact digits in TypeScript (the peg is integral and inside the
#      int64 window by construction, so BigInt(peg).toString() is
#      exact), in canon and in the Phase 5 exact JSON emitter alike --
#      JSON.stringify of the same JS number reproduces the 17-digit
#      form, so the emitter has to be part of the fix. Until that lands
#      this stays a divergence, and the window stays unpinnable.
#    RE-VERIFIED after Phase 5 and Phase 6 landed, by the agent that
#      owns this suite, against both CLIs at the exact inputs above:
#      in generated JSON and in canon alike. Neither is refused, because
#      neither is lossy. #21 THEREFORE CANNOT BE CLOSED BY PHASE 6, and
#      this entry stays. The instruction it was closed against ("close it
#      by landing that error") was written from the mistaken premise the
#      CORRECTION above dismantles; the work that would actually close it
#      is the TypeScript exact-digit rendering described there, which is
#      an engine change and not a spec change.
# NOT recorded here, because they are already documented as deliberate,
# permanent non-parity in AGENTS.md ("Known TS/Go divergences"): error
# MESSAGE text, parse-level (non-unify) canon, the canon of sources that
# are invalid in both ports, and the malformed-input acceptance edges.
# Only the substring an err-mode spec row asserts is contractual.
